cards.text: If a reader's attention is modeled as a Bernoulli draw with parameter alpha for each footnote, and if the cost of a missed footnote is the squared error in the reader's posterior, then a cleanly Bayesian author would footnote only when the expected information gain exceeds the cost of the additional eye movement. Most footnotes fail this test. The math is correct and unhelpful.

cards.text: A digression on whether Coleridge's marginalia constitute a 'work' in the editorial sense. The Princeton edition obviously thinks they do — five fat volumes, fully annotated. But marginalia as a genre resist the volume form. They are constitutively partial, occasional, and dependent on the host text. Probably belongs in a separate piece.
